title: Statutory homelessness in England: January to March 2026
summary: MHCLG's quarterly release: 135,580 households were in temporary accommodation on 31 March 2026, an increase of 1.1% from the previous quarter, and 1,000 families had been in bed and breakfast over 6 weeks, down 16.7% compared to the previous quarter. It bears on the bed and breakfast check and the six-week clock [Likely]; the market picture already reads this release.
grade_words: A2: completely reliable source; probably true

title: Temporary accommodation notification duty: guidance and funding

excerpt_original: It has already improved its procedures for the future.
title: Ombudsman decision 25 008 280: a statutory suitability review delayed
summary: The Ombudsman found fault where a council did not carry out a statutory review of a temporary placement's suitability when asked and carried out an inadequate non-statutory review instead, so the complainant lived in unsuitable accommodation for five months longer than she should have done. Remedy: an apology and a symbolic payment of £1375 (5 months at £275 a month). It bears on the eight-week review clock [Likely].
grade_words: A2: completely reliable source; probably true

excerpt_original: where a family has had to stay in unsuitable B&B accommodation in excess of the six-week legal limit
title: Ombudsman decision 25 010 543: a family past six weeks in bed and breakfast
summary: The Ombudsman found fault for the delay in moving a family out of bed and breakfast: they lived there for 28 weeks longer than the law allows. It set £100 a week as appropriate and said the council should pay £2,200; the council had already paid the £600 it offered at the first stage of the complaint. It bears on the bed and breakfast check and the six-week clock [Likely].
grade_words: A2: completely reliable source; probably true

excerpt_original: That payment should not be offset against any debts as this would stop the remedy from working as intended.
title: Ombudsman decision 25 011 724: a placement unsuitable for medical needs
summary: The council accepted the temporary accommodation was not suitable for the complainant's medical needs, and that her homeless application was delayed. It offered £5,000 and applied it to her rent arrears, which the Ombudsman said was not in accordance with its guidance: the payment should not be offset against any debts. The Ombudsman asked the council to take the £5,000 off her rent account and pay it to her directly within one month; the remedy also covers outstanding charges for the unsuitable hotel accommodation and a reminder to relevant staff. It bears on the medical needs check [Likely].
grade_words: A2: completely reliable source; probably true
